newsitem.title: UK: Asda firm as SBC Warburg repeats "buy".
newsitem.headline: Asda firm as SBC Warburg repeats "buy".

text.p: Shares in Asda Group Plc edged higher in heavy trading on Wednesday as analysts at SBC Warburg repeated a "buy" rating on the supermarket stock and set a price target of 125p which they expected to be reached by January.
The stock was up 1-1/4p at 109 by 1122 GMT in volume of 5.2 million shares, making it the second most active FTSE 100 stock.

Analyst Neil Curry at the brokerage said Asda was trading at a 15 percent discount to the rest of the market when its earnings growth was better than average, and that it was in line with the sector despite traditionally trading at a premium.

He said Tesco's Unlimited Value campaign had been aimed at Asda but had not had as big an impact as expected. And he said Asda's management had strength in depth to make up for the move to chairman of highly-rated chief executive Archie Norman.

Curry said Asda was well placed to benefit from what was expected to be a bumper Christmas season, with its high proportion on non-food sales. And it could still look forward to strong growth in margins.
